extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to BMC Medicine (medical/biomedical researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing, formatting, licensing, and submitting original research and other article types to the BMC Medicine journal, including data and peer-review expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and scope — submit to suitable journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you submit to the most suitable journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should familiarise themselves with the journal's aims and scope (BMC Medicine: general medical, clinical practice, translational medicine, public/global health, policy, and related topics) and only submit work that fits that scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript must be submitted by an author
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript can only be submitted by an author of the manuscript and may not be submitted by a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the submitting account belongs to a listed author. Third-party submissions are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article processing charge (APC) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: An article processing charge (APC) applies for each article accepted for publication; the APC price is determined from the date on which the article is accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current APC is listed (e.g. £3190 / $4490 / €3690); fee is subject to VAT/local taxes where applicable. Check country-tiered pricing pilot applicability and consult Journal pricing FAQs and open access support portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: APC waivers and discounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature offers APC waivers and discounts for corresponding authors based in the world's lowest income countries and may consider discretionary waivers for financial need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All applications for discretionary APC waivers/discounts should be made at the point of manuscript submission; requests during review or after acceptance cannot be considered. The country-tiered APC pricing pilot may supersede previous waivers/discounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and copyright (Creative Commons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open access articles are published under Creative Commons licences; BMC Medicine articles use CC BY-NC-ND or CC BY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under Creative Commons licences authors retain copyright. CC BY-NC-ND allows non-commercial sharing with attribution and forbids derivatives without permission; CC BY allows sharing and adaptation (including commercial) with attribution. Authors may explore licence variations to meet funder/institutional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: General manuscript formatting quick points
rubrics_metrics.description: Use double-line spacing; include line and page numbering; use SI units; ensure special characters are embedded; do not use page breaks in your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these basic formatting rules to ease editorial processing and reviewer reading; embedded special characters prevent loss during PDF conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable main manuscript file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: The following word processor file formats are acceptable for the main manuscript document: Microsoft Word (DOC, DOCX), Rich text format (RTF), TeX/LaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editable files are required for production. If non-editable files (e.g., PDFs) are submitted, you will be required to re-submit an editable file when requested (revisions or acceptance).

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX submissions and source files
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to use the Springer Nature LaTeX template; a PDF of your manuscript will be compiled during submission using pdfLaTeX and TexLive 2021.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All relevant editable source files must be uploaded during submission; failing to submit these source files will cause unnecessary delays in production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and materials availability expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly encouraged or required to provide all datasets on which conclusions rely, either by depositing in public repositories or as supporting/additional files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide datasets in machine-readable formats (spreadsheets rather than PDFs). Where community expectations exist for public repositories, archiving there is mandatory. Include an 'Availability of data and materials' section in the manuscript with required wording or indication of inclusion as additional files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required format for 'Availability of data and materials' section
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard format is provided for the data availability statement, e.g. 'The dataset(s) supporting the conclusions of this article is(are) available in the [repository name] repository, [unique persistent identifier and hyperlink to dataset(s) in https:// format].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If data are included as additional files use the specified wording: 'The dataset(s) supporting the conclusions of this article is(are) included within the article (and its additional file(s)).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Data citation and identifiers (Force11 endorsement)
rubrics_metrics.description: BioMed Central endorses the Force11 Data Citation Principles and requires that all publicly available datasets be fully referenced in the reference list with an accession number or unique identifier such as a DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For databases, state the web/ftp address and any restrictions to its use by non-academics. Use persistent identifiers when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For software, include: Project name; Project home page; Archived version DOI or unique identifier (e.g., Zenodo); Operating system(s); Programming language; Other requirements; License; Any restrictions to use by non-academics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient metadata to enable reuse and reproducibility. Example formats are given to follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference inclusion — what may be cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Only articles, clinical trial registration records and abstracts that have been published or are in press, or are available through public e-print/preprint servers, may be cited in the reference list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unpublished abstracts, unpublished data and personal communications should not be included in the reference list but may be included in the text as 'unpublished observations' or 'personal communications' with permission; obtaining permission to quote is the author's responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference formatting and web link handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Web links and URLs should be given a reference number and included in the reference list rather than within the text. Provide full details including title, URL and date accessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Instructions for Authors for the specific article type for the required reference style. Authors may use reference management software to ensure correct formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures — numbering, multi-panel and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be numbered in the order they are first mentioned; multi-panel figures should be submitted as a single composite file containing all parts; figure files should be uploaded in the order they are mentioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure figures are uploaded in correct orientation and order to facilitate production; cite in text in sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure titles, legends and keys constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure titles (max 15 words) and legends (max 300 words) should be provided in the main manuscript, not in the graphic file. Figure keys should be incorporated into the graphic, not into the legend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep titles concise and legends informative but within limits so the final PDF layout remains compliant. Place keys in graphics to maintain consistency across formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure cropping, fonts, line width and legibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure should be closely cropped to minimise white space; all fonts must be embedded; all lines should be wider than 0.25 pt when constrained to standard figure widths; design figures so text is legible at final sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design at the expected final dimensions to ensure labels and symbols are readable after resizing by production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure size, resolution and file size limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Web figures: width 600 px (standard) or 1200 px (high resolution). Final PDF widths: 85 mm (half page) or 170 mm (full page); maximum height 225 mm. Image resolution approx. 300 dpi at final size. Individual figure files should not exceed 10 MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure images meet resolution and size constraints; keep file sizes reasonable and choose suitable formats to meet quality without excessive file size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted figure file formats and compression guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted file types: EPS, PDF, Microsoft Word (single page), PowerPoint (single page), TIFF, JPEG, PNG, BMP, CDX (ChemDraw). Vector figures should preferably be PDF; TIFF saved with LZW compression; JPEG saved at maximum quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimise conversions between file types to avoid quality loss. Use lossless compression where possible (e.g., TIFF LZW) and avoid repeated JPEG recompression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission for previously published figures/tables
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the responsibility of the author(s) to obtain permission from the copyright holder to reproduce figures or tables previously published elsewhere; permission should be indicated in the figure legend and original source included in the reference list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For open access publishing, authors must obtain permission if including images from non-open-access sources; failure to secure permission may prevent inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table numbering, placement and file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables should be numbered and cited in the text in sequence using Arabic numerals. Tables less than one A4/Letter page can be placed inline; larger tables can be placed at the end of the document or uploaded as additional files. Tabular data as additional files can be .xls or .csv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate where large tables should appear if placed at the end, and cite additional-file tables in the main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table titles, legends and formatting constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Table titles (max 15 words) above the table and legends (max 300 words) below the table. Tables should not be embedded as figures or spreadsheet files but formatted using the 'Table object' function. Color and shading may not be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parts of tables may be highlighted using superscript, numbering, lettering, symbols or bold; explain meanings in the legend. Do not use commas to indicate numerical values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional files — content, naming, metadata and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can provide datasets, tables, movies or other information as additional files; all additional files will be published with the accepted article. Additional files should be named 'Additional file 1' etc and be cited in sequence within the main text. For each additional file include file name, format, title and description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include patient consent forms, language-editing certificates, or revised main manuscripts with tracked changes as additional files unless requested. Do not include individual participant details. Maximum file size per additional file is 20 MB. Files will be virus-scanned on submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language quality and editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting work in well‑written English gives the best chance for editors and reviewers to understand it and evaluate it fairly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may use the publisher's language editing services, solicit colleague review, or use the offered free language quality checker (AJE). Using these services is not required and does not guarantee selection for peer review or acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A cover letter should include: an explanation of why your manuscript should be published in BMC Medicine; an explanation of any issues relating to journal policies; a declaration of any potential competing interests; confirmation that all authors have approved the manuscript; confirmation that the content has not been published or submitted elsewhere. If submitting to a special issue, name it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow additional article-type instructions for any further cover letter requirements. Include any requested information to speed editorial assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer suggestions and prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: In the cover letter, authors may suggest potential peer reviewers and provide institutional email addresses or identifiers (ORCID, Scopus ID). Authors may also name people they prefer not to review their manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide verifiable contact details; intentionally falsifying reviewer details will result in rejection and possible misconduct investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review criteria used by reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically two or more experts evaluate each manuscript based on three main criteria: scientific robustness (methodology and whether data support conclusions), originality (does the research duplicate already published work), and clarity (is the manuscript clear and coherent enough for publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors base decisions on reviewers' reports and may consult the editorial board. Reviewers and editors are required to declare competing interests and may be excluded if conflicts exist. BMC Medicine operates a transparent peer review system where reviewer reports are published (reviewer not named) under a CC BY license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript transfer process
rubrics_metrics.description: If a manuscript is not accepted in the chosen journal, a transfer provides a convenient way to resubmit files and reviewer comments to another journal within the publisher's portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer offers give choice and can save time (no reformatting necessary). Transfers are not completed without the author's input; authors can decline or withdraw transfers at any point by contacting the Transfer Desk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion and dissemination encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: Publisher marketing teams promote accepted articles via email updates, alerts, social media, blogs and press releases; authors are encouraged to promote their work via email, social media, conferences and institutional offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotion may increase views, downloads and impact. Authors should comply with journal/publisher policies when promoting material.
